title: HISTORY PAPER 1 FORM
text:
311/1
 HISTORY AND GOVERNMENT PAPER 1
 MARKING SCHEME
 1. -Two aspects of history
 - Economic history social history political history
 2. the original homeland of the river –lake nilotes of Kenya (2x1)= 2mks
 - Bahr-el –ghazal in Southern Sudan 91X10 = 1MK
 3. Two units of the pre-colonial period administration of Borana .
 - Clan
 - Moieties (2x1) 2mks
 4 . Main factors that led to the growth of towns along Kenyan coast
 - Trade (1x1) =0.1 mks
 5, Two advantages of using arbitration as a method of solving conflict
 - One can choose their own arbitrator
 - It is private and confidential
 - You choose your own rules
 6. Two areas required by the British as a result of Anglo-German treaty of 1890
 - Uganda
 - Witu
 - Kenya ( any 2 = 2mks)
 7. Two reasons why the Akamba were defeated by the British
 - British had superior weapons
 - disunity among the Akamba/some sections collaborated
 - natural calamities
 - Akamba lacked trained army or weapons any ( 2x1) = 2mks
 8. Two reasons why Africans refused to labour during colonial periods
 - wages were low or unattractive
 -Poor and harsh working conditions
 -Were bitter that settlers had taken African land
 9. One positive result of the Mau mau resistant
 - Political reforms were initiated
 - attracted British international community about the situation in Kenya
 - speeded up the march to independence
 - powers and influence of settlers were reduced (1x1 )1 mk
 10. Trade union which organized workers strike of 1947in Kenya
 - AWU- African Workers Union (1x1) 1 mk
 11. Main reason why KANU refused to form government in 1961 elections
 - because Kenyatta its leader was still in prison (1x1) 1 mk
 12. Challenges faced by President Moi in 1982
 - the attempted coup (1x1) 1mk
 13, External factors that led to growth of multiparty system in Kenya in the early 1990s
 - Development in Easter Europe e.g end of cold war, collapse of communist Russia
 - Success of multipartism in other parts of African e.g Togo and Zambia
 - Pressure from multi and bilateral or donors Any ( 2x1) =2mks
 14 Two reasons why cultural activities are important in Kenya
 - For entertainment
 - Briefing people together
 - Source of employment
 - Promote patriotism
 - Educating the masses Any( 2x1) = 2mks)
 15. One class of human rights
 - civil and political rights
 - Socio-economic and cultural rights
 - Solidarity rights (1x1)= 1mk
 16. identify one type of government expenditure
 - Recurrent
 - Capital (1x1) =1mk
 17. Chief executive officer in the county
 - Governor (1x1) =1mk
 SECTION B 45 MARK
 18 a) Five social function of oloibon among the Nandi
 - Conducted religious ceremonies
 - Blessed the warriors before going to war
 - Prophesized about future events
 - Was chief medicine man
 - Was a rainmaker
 - Acted as an intermediary between God and the people
 - Was a ritual expert Any ( 5x1) = 05 mks
 b) Political organization of the Nandi
 - basic political unit was the clan
 - several clans joined together to form a longer and highest political unit- the prophet
 -the clan was governed by junior council of elders who settled minor disputes
 - Each prophet was controlled by a council of elders who decided in serious mattes
 - it settled major disputes as it was the highest court
 - they had an influential institution of the Orkoiyot who also played an important political roe as advising the
 council of elders Any ( 5x2)= 10 mks
 19 a) reasons why Christian missionaries established mission in Kenya
 i) Mission stations were established by Christian missionaries to serve as centers for converting Africans
 ii) To serve as centers where Africans would be taught basic literacy to enable them to read the bible
 iii) To teach Africans new methods of carpentry, farming and masonry
 iv) To train catechists who would in turn facilitate the spread of Christianity
 v) To use them as the centers for the spread of Western European culture
 vi) To serve as settlements for freed slaves and other displaced peoples
 vii) Serve as centers for pacification of Africans/centers to promote European colonization
 viii) Serve as a base where Europeans missionaries could co-operate from. 5x1 = 5mks
 b) what factors undermined Christian missionaries activities in Kenya during the 19 th century
 i) Hostility by believers of traditional religion who saw missionaries as a threat to their beliefs and
 cultural practices
 ii) Opposition by leaders of Islamic faith and other leaders whose interest were to advance their religion in
 the region
 iii) Harsh climate coupled with tropical diseases
 iv) Inadequate funds and supplies such as food
 v) Inadequate personnel to carry out missionary activities
 vi) Rivalry among different Christian groups
 vii) Communication nbarrier /lack of common language of communication to facilitate interaction with and
 conversion of Africans
 viii) Strict Christian doctrines which were incompatible with traditional beliefs and practices
 ix) Limited transport and communication facilities
 x) Vastness of areas covered by individual missionaries 3x1 = 3mks
 20. three methods used by the colonial government to acquire labor for settlers in Kenya
 - colonial government alienated fertile lands from Africans
 - imposed payment of tax on Africans
 - denied them the right to grow cash crops
 - created native reserves 6x2 = 12 mks
 b) impact of colonial land policies
 - Africans lost their land and became jobless
 - the loss led to African nationalism and resentment to the colonists
 - the landless were settled in small ,infertile native researves which encouraged the squatter way of survival
 - rural-urban migration
 - introduction to the kipande system to restrict movement of Africans
 - urbanization led to breakdown of African traditional setup
 - over-population in towns led to lack of employment
 - moral decay due to lack of privacy in the slums 6x2 = 12 mks
 21. Five reasons why the government of Kenya adopted the sectional paper NO 10 of 1965
 - to ensure equal opportunities in Kenya
 - to promote democracy
 - to ensure the resources are used for the benefits of the society and its members
 - to encourage various forms of ownership of property
 - to promote freedom from disease, ignorance and poverty
 - to promote freedom of conscience and human dignity 5x1 = 5 mks
 b) Challenges facing opposition parties in Kenya since 1992
 - defectiveness
 - inefficient funding
 -Wrangling of leaders
 -ethnicity
 - interference by the government
 - lack of internal democracy
 - lack of numbers
 - lack of numbers (tyranny of numbers) in parliament 6x2 = 12 mks
 SECTION C 30MARKS
 22 a) three aspects of democracy
 - Political aspect
 - Social
 - Economic
 b) Benefits of democracy
 - promote citizen participation in elections
 - enables good and quality representation
 Balances the liberty of the individual and the state
 Promotes peace and stability
 Promotes equality
 Leads to higher production /increased income/economic participation
 Safeguards human rights
 23 a) superior courts
 - Supreme courts
 - Court of appeal
 - High court 3X1 = 3 MKS
 b) Functions of the chief justice
 - head of judiciary
 - chairperson of the judicial service commission
 - advises the president on promotional or remval of judges
 -Presents fees to be judged by the courts
 - head of supreme court
 - swears in the president and the cabinet
 - main defender of the constitution 6X2 = 12 MKS
